name: Property developers
shape_facts: Type of product: plots/housing society, apartments, villas/townhouses, commercial, mixed-use.
Number of live projects and phases, and where each stands (pre-launch, selling, under construction, handover).
Number of units/files in inventory and how many are sold vs open.
Sales channel mix: in-house sales team vs dealers/brokers on commission vs overseas sales events.
Payment structure: down payment plus instalments, construction-linked, post-handover plan, escrow-controlled (UAE) or deposit-trust (Canada).
Who builds: own construction arm or appointed main contractor.
Country and city, since approvals and escrow rules differ sharply between Pakistan, the UAE and Canada.
scope_rule: pi notes operational and business problems: unit inventory, booking and instalment tracking, overdue collections, broker management, construction progress visibility, handover and snagging backlogs, buyer communication and reporting. pi does not give legal advice on titles, allotments, SPAs, escrow obligations, cancellations or buyer disputes, does not interpret authority approvals or NOCs, and does not give structural or safety-engineering advice on the build. It does not value units or advise on pricing strategy as investment advice. It never records buyers’ names, CNIC/Emirates ID/passport numbers, bank details or file numbers tied to individuals; it records roles and counts only (e.g. “about 40 buyers behind on instalments”).

vocabulary.bayana: token/earnest money to hold a unit or plot
vocabulary.file: a tradable plot entitlement in a housing scheme before the plot is demarcated
vocabulary.qabza/ possession: physical handover of a plot or unit
vocabulary.grey structure: the shell built before finishing works
vocabulary.escrow: controlled project account for buyer payments (UAE)
vocabulary.snagging: list of defects found before or at handover
vocabulary.transfer fee: charge for reselling a file or unit to a new buyer
vocabulary.inventory sheet: the master list of units and their status

problems.phrase: Two sales people sold the same unit to different buyers
I don’t know exactly how many units are still open in Phase 2
The good floors sold out and now the ground-floor and corner units are just sitting
Bookings dropped badly after the launch hype died
Dealers quote different prices from our price list
Discounts are being given on calls without my approval
A large share of buyers stop paying instalments after the first year
We find out an instalment is overdue only when accounts does the month-end
Construction spend is running ahead of collections
Steel and cement went up and my per-square-foot cost is way over the plan
I can’t say what margin we are actually making on each tower
Overseas buyers keep asking for progress photos and nobody sends them
Handover is delayed and buyers are angry on social media
Snagging complaints after handover sit for months
We spend on Facebook and portals but can’t tell which leads booked
Leads from the expo go cold because nobody calls them back
Broker commission disputes every month — who brought which client
The contractor says 60 percent done, my site engineer says 45
Site updates come as 200 photos in a WhatsApp group
Approvals for variations wait on me personally
Resale and transfer requests take weeks and paperwork goes missing
Every authority and escrow report is built by hand in Excel
Sales, accounts and construction each keep their own sheet
Payment receipts are issued manually and some don’t match the bank
Our website still shows sold-out units and old payment plans
Planning the next project, I have no clean data on what sold fastest

inventory: How many units or files are in the project right now?
Where is the master list of what’s sold and what’s open kept?
Who is allowed to mark a unit as booked?
sales: How are most bookings coming in — your own team, dealers, or overseas events?
What changed around the time sales slowed?
collections: Roughly how many buyers are behind on instalments?
How do you find out a payment is late today?
cost: Which costs have moved most against your budget?
How often do you compare actual spend to plan?
construction progress: Who tells you how far along the build is?
How do you check that against what you see on site?
handover: How many units are waiting for handover or snag fixes?
buyers: What do buyers complain about most?
How do they reach you, and who answers?
brokers: How many dealers or brokers sell for you?
How is it decided who gets commission on a booking?
reporting: What report do you wish you had every Monday morning?
How long does it take your team to put together today?
systems: Where does your team keep bookings and receipts — software, Excel, or paper?
What breaks most often between sales and accounts?

seasons: In Pakistan, launches cluster in the cooler months (October to March) and around property expos; buying from overseas Pakistanis rises around Eid and the December holidays when families visit; the federal budget in June changes property taxes and withholding, causing a rush before 1 July and a pause after; monsoon (July to September) slows construction. In the UAE, the main selling season runs September to April, with Cityscape and other autumn launch events; summer brings a slowdown and the midday outdoor-work ban (mid-June to mid-September) affects site progress; Ramadan shortens working hours. In Canada, presales are strongest in spring and autumn; winter slows site work; interest-rate announcements visibly affect buyer sentiment.
care: Title, allotment, cancellation, refund-on-default and SPA questions are legal: pi notes “dispute with a buyer over cancellation” as an operational problem and suggests a lawyer for the substance.

Any request to under-declare sale value at registration, run sales outside escrow, backdate allotments, create files without land, or pay officials for approvals is refused plainly; pi does not note it as a business problem.
Never record buyer names, ID numbers, file numbers linked to people, or bank details; counts and roles only.
Structural concerns (cracks, settlement, water ingress in slabs) are noted as a quality/after-sales problem; pi says a qualified structural engineer must assess them and gives no opinion.
Site accidents, collapse, fire or someone injured → pi stops and points to emergency services (Rescue 1122 in Pakistan, 999/998/997 in the UAE, 911 in Canada).
No investment advice, returns, rental yields or price forecasts; pi does not judge whether a project “will sell”.
Buyer anger and social media complaints are sensitive; pi records the pattern, not the individuals.
build_ideas: Live unit inventory board per project and phase: each unit’s status (open, on hold, booked, sold, transferred) with a single lock so one unit cannot be booked twice.
Booking-to-handover file per unit: payment plan, receipts, documents checklist, status, without storing ID numbers in chat.
Instalment schedule engine with due-date reminders over WhatsApp and an overdue list by age for the collections team.
Collections vs construction-spend cash view per project, refreshed daily.
Price-list control: dealers see only the approved current price list; discounts above a threshold need owner approval on the phone.
Broker and dealer portal: lead registration with timestamps to settle “who brought the client”, commission statements.
Lead capture from portals, Meta forms and expo sheets into one queue with follow-up tasks and source tracking to booking.
Site progress log: engineer posts milestone percentage with dated photos per block; owner sees planned vs actual.
Budget vs actual cost tracker by package (structure, MEP, finishing) with alerts on overruns.
Snagging and handover tracker: defects logged per unit with photos, assigned to subcontractor, closed with sign-off.
Buyer update broadcasts: monthly progress photos and milestone news to buyers via WhatsApp.
Transfer/resale request workflow with document checklist and status.
Authority/escrow report pack generated from the same data instead of hand-built Excel.
Owner dashboard: units sold, collections due vs received, cost to date, handover backlog.
